title: Quantum Speedups for Testing Similar Means
authors: Chengshen Gao, Yongzhen Xu, Shenggen Zheng, Lvzhou Li
abstract: Property testing of distributions is a central topic in information theory, learning theory, and statistics. While quantum algorithms are known to offer significant speedups for property testing of a single distribution or a pair of distributions, it is unclear whether quantum algorithms provide speedups for property testing of $m$ ($m\geq 3$) distributions. This work focuses on quantum algorithms for testing whether $m$ distributions have similar means or are $ε$-far from mean similarity under two models. In the query model, the algorithm can choose which distribution to sample from, whereas in the sampling model, the distributions are selected uniformly. We design quantum algorithms with complexities $\tilde{O}(1/ε)$ (the $\tilde{O}$ notation hides poly-logarithmic factors) and $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{m}/ε)$ in the query and sampling models, respectively, achieving quadratic speedups over the classical counterparts. We further establish quantum lower bounds of $Ω\left(1/ε\right)$ and $Ω\rbra{m^{1/3}+\frac{m^{1/4}}ε}$ for the query model and the sampling model, demonstrating the optimality of our quantum algorithms in terms of the dependence on $ε$ up to logarithmic factors.
summary: This paper develops quantum algorithms to test whether multiple probability distributions share similar means, extending property testing beyond pairs of distributions. It achieves provable quadratic speedups over classical methods in both query and sampling access models. The results establish optimal complexity bounds for this multi-distribution mean similarity testing problem.
main_problem: The work addresses the open question of whether quantum algorithms provide speedups for property testing when comparing $m \ge 3$ distributions, specifically testing if they share similar means.
main_result: They design quantum algorithms achieving complexities $	ilde{O}(1/\epsilon)$ (query model) and $	ilde{O}(\sqrt{m}/\epsilon)$ (sampling model), demonstrating quadratic speedups over classical bounds and establishing corresponding lower bounds.
method: The approach involves adapting techniques like Quantum Amplitude Estimation (QAE) to estimate extremal feasible means under $\ell_1$-bounded perturbations, avoiding direct mean estimation which is insufficient.
model_or_system: The problem is framed abstractly using quantum access models: the Query Model (unitary $O_A$) and the Sampling Model (unitary $O_B$). The underlying objects are classical probability distributions over $\{0, \dots, n\}$.
key_observables: Mean of a distribution $\mu(D)$, $\ell_1$ distance between distributions, and the deviation parameter $\epsilon$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on structural separation lemmas that characterize collections of distributions far from mean similarity, enabling the use of QAE/QME.
figures_summary: Table 1 summarizes the derived classical versus quantum complexities for both query and sampling models.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem in two quantum access models. It then develops specialized quantum algorithms (like $\ell_1$QFME) to estimate necessary bounds, culminating in theorems that prove the optimal complexity bounds for testing mean similarity in both models.
why_interesting: This work directly tackles the boundary between classical and quantum computational advantages in a fundamental area of information theory—property testing—which is highly relevant for understanding the limits of quantum computation.
